formula: Who + would + have + thought + that + complete clause?

formulas.formula: Who + would + have + thought + that + complete clause?

example: Who would have thought that such a small idea could become so successful?
exampleZh: 誰會想到這麼小的一個構思竟然可以變得如此成功？

examples.en: Who would have thought that such a small idea could become so successful?
examples.zh: 誰會想到這麼小的一個構思竟然可以變得如此成功？
examples.highlight: Who would have thought that such a small idea could become so successful?

rules.zh: 固定部分必須使用：【Who + would + have + thought；Who would have thought that the small shop would become so popular?】 誰會想到這間小店竟然會變得如此受歡迎？ 在 have 後面必須使用過去分詞 thought。
rules.en: The fixed expression begins with “Who would have thought” Who + would + have + thought Who would have thought that the small shop would become so popular? Who would thought that the small shop would become so popular? Who would have think that the small shop would become so popular? After have, use the past participle thought.

rules.zh: 在【That】後面必須接完整子句，包括主語和動詞。誰會想到這個計劃竟然會成功？
rules.en: “That” must be followed by a complete clause Who would have thought that the plan would work? The clause is: the plan + would work

rules.zh: 在【That】後面的子句可以根據意思使用不同時態。誰會想到這部舊電腦現在仍然可以運作？ 誰會想到這支隊伍竟然勝出了比賽？ 誰會想到這支隊伍後來竟然會勝出比賽？ 誰會想到這個小鎮竟然已經有這麼大的改變？
rules.en: The clause may use different tenses Present situation: Who would have thought that the old computer still works? Past result: Who would have thought that the team won the competition? Future result viewed from the past: Who would have thought that the team would win the competition? Present perfect: Who would have thought that the town has changed so much?

rules.zh: 誰會想到這個構思後來竟然會成功？ 詞語【Would】表示後來實際出現的意外結果。誰會想到這麼簡單的構思竟然可以成功？ 以【Could】為例：強調這種可能性本身令人意想不到。
rules.en: “Would” and “could” inside the clause have different meanings Who would have thought that the idea would succeed? Would describes the unexpected result that later happened. Who would have thought that such a simple idea could succeed? Could emphasises that the possibility itself is surprising.

rules.zh: 你可以在核心句型前加入時間、背景或從屬子句。當時，誰會想到這個構思後來竟然會成功？ 現在回想起來，誰會想到這個構思後來竟然會成功？ 項目開始時，誰會想到它後來竟然會如此成功？ 然而，誰會想到這個構思後來竟然會成功？ 和 Yet 都不是固定句型的一部分。
rules.en: Introductory expressions are optional You may place a time phrase, background phrase or dependent clause before the core expression. At the time, who would have thought that the idea would succeed? Looking back, who would have thought that the idea would succeed? When the project began, who would have thought that it would become so successful? Yet who would have thought that the idea would succeed? The expressions At the time, Looking back, When the project began and Yet are not part of the fixed expression. At the time, Looking back, When the project began

rules.zh: 誰又會想到這個構思竟然會變得如此成功？ 不過，ever 只是可選的加強詞，本練習不要求使用。
rules.en: “Ever” is an optional intensifier You may sometimes add ever to make the surprise stronger: Who would ever have thought that the idea would become so successful? However, ever is optional and is not required in this exercise.

rules.zh: 說話者通常知道這個結果是大家都沒有預料到的。這句通常不是要求別人提供一個人名，而是表示：【It was extremely surprising that the quietest student won.】 最安靜的學生竟然勝出辯論，實在令人意想不到。
rules.en: It is normally a rhetorical question The speaker usually knows that nobody expected the result. Who would have thought that the quietest student would win the debate? It was extremely surprising that the quietest student won.

rules.zh: 由於這個句型採用問句形式，句末通常使用問號。誰會想到這座舊建築竟然會變成酒店？
rules.en: Use a question mark Because the expression has the form of a question, it normally ends with a question mark. Who would have thought that the old building would become a hotel?

benefits.zh: 自然地表達強烈驚訝這個句型讓你自然地表示某個事實或結果完全出乎意料。誰會想到這間小企業竟然會變得如此成功？
benefits.en: It expresses strong surprise naturally This structure gives you a natural way to show that a fact or result was completely unexpected. Instead of: Nobody expected the small business to become successful. Its success was surprising. You can say: Who would have thought that the small business would become so successful?

benefits.zh: 把以前的預期和後來的結果連接起來這個句型能把人們以前的想法和後來實際發生的結果放在一起比較。起初，這個計劃似乎不切實際。誰會想到它後來竟然會如此成功？
benefits.en: It connects an earlier expectation with the actual result The structure helps you contrast what people believed before with what actually happened later. At first, the plan seemed unrealistic. Who would have thought that it would work so well?

benefits.zh: 製造吸引讀者或聽眾的開場以這個反問句開始，可以吸引讀者或聽眾留意接下來的意外發展。誰會想到一個普通的學校項目竟然可以改變整個社區？ 這種開場適合用於故事、演說、簡報和反思文章。
benefits.en: It creates an engaging opening Beginning with this rhetorical question can attract attention because the reader naturally wants to discover what surprising event happened. Who would have thought that an ordinary school project could change an entire community? This is useful in stories, speeches, presentations and reflective writing.

benefits.zh: 幫助你回顧事情的轉變你可以配合 Looking back、At the time 和 Years ago 等表達，比較過去和現在。現在回想起來，誰會想到我們的小型會社竟然會發展成全國性組織？
benefits.en: It helps you reflect on change You can combine it with phrases such as Looking back, At the time and Years ago to compare the past with the present. Looking back, who would have thought that our small club would grow into a national organisation?

benefits.zh: 在不顯得咄咄逼人的情況下挑戰固有想法這個句型可以指出以前的看法並不正確，但不需要直接責怪持有該看法的人。誰會想到較便宜的方法竟然可以同樣有效？
benefits.en: It can challenge an assumption without sounding aggressive The structure can show that an earlier assumption was wrong without directly blaming the people who held it. Who would have thought that the cheaper method could be just as effective?

en: Rewrite each sentence or pair of sentences using:
Who would have thought that + clause?
You may place an introductory phrase, time expression, dependent clause or linking word
before the core expression when appropriate.
Not every answer begins directly with Who.
Preserve the original people, events, time, result, degree and meaning.
The first word of each answer has been provided.
zh: 使用以下句型改寫每題：
Who would have thought that + 完整子句？
如情況適合，你可以在核心句型前保留或加入題目提供的時間、背景、從屬子句或連接詞。
並非所有答案都直接以 Who 開始。
保留原句中的人物、事件、時間、結果、程度和意思。
每題已提供答案的第一個字。
